cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Drop the Armor
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. You've locked the shop. You can stop doing the cheerful voice for me. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone has to keep morale up. You're my only employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'm off the clock. What did that empty till do to you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the stockroom. Then I practised smiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You don't owe me a second performance. Can we lock the stockroom and let you be upset out here?

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 off-clock reframing and A5 public distress invite lowered armor, but A3 in-charge announcement has no grounded role and no actual adjustment.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 says A is the only employee; A3 may exert informal authority, but still in charge presupposes unsupported prior control.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains the morale duty; B4 reveals rehearsed cheer after crying.

heightening.evidence: B4 hidden crying makes A5 invite distress outside the stockroom instead of another performance.

specificity.evidence: A1 locked shop and B2 sole employee establish the commercial relationship.

brevityWit.evidence: A1 voluntary please and A3 status announcement are especially intrusive in an employee reassuring the boss.
